about: Every dimension the F/A-18C build uses, with its source (an id in references.json) and where in it. Values are in the source's own units; the build converts. Stations (FS) are inches aft of the fuselage datum, waterlines (WL) inches above it (WL 100 is the fuselage reference line), buttlines (BL) inches from the centreline, positive to starboard. Angles round the fuselage (theta) follow TM-101724 figure 3: looking aft, 0 is the bottom centreline, 180 the top, 90 starboard and 270 port. A fact taken from the old model, as a last resort, names the old model as its source and says why no other source had it (air-fa18c.md #2).

length.also: hatp figure 2 (56.00 ft); tp209033 figure 2 (56.0 ft)

exhaust.note: nose apex to the engine exhaust plane
exhaust.also: tp3478 PDF page 6 (54.4 ft, nose to exhaust nozzle exit plane, full scale)

spread.note: 37 ft 6 in, without missiles. hatp figure 2 gives the reference span as 37.417 ft

fins.note: 15 ft 3 in, to the top of the fins
fins.also: tp209033 figure 2 (15.3 ft, on its gear)

canopy.note: 10 ft 6 in, to the top of the closed canopy

gravity.note: moment reference at 25% of the mean aerodynamic chord

station.note: moment reference at 25% of the mean aerodynamic chord, WL 100.00, BL 0

leading.note: leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord (11.52 ft)

apex.also: tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82); tm110216 figure 3.1 (FS 59.9); tp3111 figure 7 (FS 60.60)

droop.note: the nosecone centreline is depressed 5.6 deg; the first three stations are canted forward to match

sections.note: from the LEX-fuselage junction to the LEX leading edge

graph.note: LEX local span on the full-scale jet, read off the graph to about 1 in; runs about 1 in above tm101724's three stations

fence.unit: in, FS in, BL in, deg
fence.where: figure 7, PDF page 33; text PDF page 8
fence.note: the 0.06-scale model's fence, in full-scale inches: normal to the LEX surface at its leading edge, about 25 deg from vertical

hardware.note: the full-scale fence fitted to fleet jets; its lengths differ from tp3111's model fence, so the 2020s photos settle the shape

gun.note: the gun port exits, on the upper centreline near FS 122

probe.note: the in-flight refuelling probe doors, upper starboard side

pitot.note: the two production pitot-static probes, lower fuselage

ecm.note: two elliptical ECM antenna covers on the research jet; confirm on the 2020s reference airframe

scale.note: the 0.06-scale wind-tunnel model's three-view: b = 2.245 ft, length 3.360 ft, S = 1.44 ft2, mean chord 0.691 ft

surfaces.about: Surface positions NATOPS gives for each flap setting, in degrees down, and the mechanical limits (limits).

ground.note: HALF or FULL on the ground; AUTO with weight on wheels is 0

fixed.note: GAIN ORIDE with HALF or FULL

check.where: ground checklist, spin recovery mode check
check.note: 33 +/- 1 deg down with the spin recovery mode engaged: the most the flaps travel in NATOPS

differential.note: up to +/-3 deg below 30,000 ft above Mach 0.7

half.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

full.note: aileron droop; 0 with the wings unlocked

trim.note: takeoff trim drives the stabilator to 12 deg nose up

limits.about: Mechanical position and rate limits, deg and deg/s, from tp209033 table 2 (PDF page 16), which states they are the basic F-18A/B's. tm110216 table 6.2 (PDF page 99) gives the HARV's aileron as 25 up and 42 down.

waterline.note: the fuselage reference line corresponds to WL 100.0 on the airplane

buttline.note: BL 0 is the centreline; BL grows to starboard (Y is right of the c.g.)

apex.note: the fuselage reference line (WL 100) is drawn through the nose apex and on aft past the stabilator; tp209033 figure 2 points WL 100 at the stabilator

chord.note: mean aerodynamic chord, projected; tp209033 and hatp give 11.52 ft (138.24 in) as the reference chord

root.note: NACA 65A with a sharp leading edge, at wing station 56.876 (cr201687 table 1: modified NACA 65A, 5.0%)

tip.note: cr201687 table 1 agrees (3.5%); secondary sources' 65A003 is not supported

span.note: span station of the wingtip at the launcher rail, on a sketch; the reference semispan is 224.5 in

lef.note: each inboard leading-edge flap is 36.5% of the total LEF area, each outboard 13.5%; one actuator drives both

areas.note: totals for both sides. cr3608's 1/10-scale model gives 0.19, 0.55 and 0.62 ft2, which scale to 19, 55 and 62

exposed.note: reference span of the exposed panels

area.note: theoretical exposed, both sides; tm4772 table 1 gives 88.26 unmodified

toe.note: toe out, as the model table gives it

top.note: the fin tip 11.34 in above the fuselage reference line on the 1/10-scale model. Anchored at the apex, the HATP side view draws it about 4 in higher and its canopy top at WL 163, which this figure also draws

forebody.note: the McDonnell Douglas drawing's forebody height and width, read off the graphs to about 1 in; agrees with tm101724's sections

buttline.note: TLOC: each engine axis 2.33 ft either side of the centreline at the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56), where the figure draws it

angle.note: EPS: the engine axis's angle to the aircraft's x axis in plan. The axes converge aft: hatp figure 2's top view draws the nozzles at BL 19.5 either side, nearly touching, as photo dvids9820758 shows, which 2 deg of convergence from 28 in at FS 458.56 gives (19.3 in at FS 707)

thrust.note: DXTHRS: the thrust point's distance aft of the aerodynamic reference centre (FS 458.56)

inlet.note: hydraulic diameter of the inlet duct entrance

canopy.note: how much bigger the two-seat canopy is than the single-seat one; tp209033 figure 2 draws the two-seat jet

gravity.aircraft: HARV phase 1, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
HARV phases 2-3, 60% fuel, clean, gear up
F-18B SRA, 66% fuel, clean, gear up

airfoils.note: NACA 65A basic thickness forms: half-thickness y at chordwise station x, both in percent of chord. Another thickness takes y/t interpolated linearly in t between the tabulated forms (TR-84's own method, by its cross plots); above 5% the 5% ratios hold, which TR-84's 63-series cross plots show moving under 2% between 5% and 6%.

layout.about: Placements no source states, fitted to the NASA three-views with the published planforms (views.py's masks, the side view anchored at the apex on WL 100). Each says what it was fitted to. Provisional until the reference airframe's photos confirm them.

wing.where: figure 5, PDF page 31 (traced by views.py), with hatp figure 2's side view for the keel. The anhedral: photos.py's cameras and tips.py (rotating the wing about the junction; deflections fitted, or held at rest in flight) over the ground photo dvids9820799 and the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145, their cameras solved with the rest (fin tips within 0.3 in)
wing.note: the wing's chord plane at the LEX-wing junction (BL 54.5, FS 404.05): the FS 357 section's LEX tip stands 31 in above its keel, and the keel is at WL 82.5. The anhedral is the photos', the jet parked (the user's choice, 2026-10-30): cr201687's -3 deg (wing.dihedral) leaves the tips' trailing corners about 5 in low in the ground photo (+-2 in or more: its flaps and ailerons droop) and 10 in low in three in-flight photos (8.7-10.3 leaving each out), the difference the wing bending up at 1 g (task: wing flex). Rotating the wing about the junction fits the flight photos a little better than raising it, and the junction itself measures no higher (4 in lower, +-2.3, two photos). The HATP front view draws the outer wing about 10 in higher

stabilator.where: figure 2, top view; natops 1.1.2 for the length; the waterline from the in-flight photos dvids8901347, dvids7487368 and dvids6690145 (tips.py, deflections held at rest, the cameras photos.py solved)
stabilator.note: the root leading edge of the exposed panel (BL 41.6: the 21.6 ft span less the 14.67 ft exposed span), placed so the tips' trailing edges fall at FS 732.5, the 56 ft overall length from the apex (overall.length, the aftmost point); the top view's leading edge at BL 80-120 then lies within about 2 in. WL 106.8: the in-flight photos put the tips' leading corners 6.8 in above where cr3608 figure 3's and tp209033 figure 2's WL 100 had them (6.3-7.7 leaving each photo out; 4-7.5 with trim free), the root then at the engine axes' height (WL 106), where the real stabilators sit; the HATP side view draws them about 10 in higher. The spindle is not published

fin.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): the fin tips' four corners in 6-9 photos (+-1.8 in along, +-0.3 in across)
fin.note: leading edge at root and tip, on cr201687's planform, sweep and cant: the photos put the tips 8 in further aft and 7 in further outboard than the HATP views were fitted to give (FS 613.6, BL 71.4), the HATP side view's own top trailing corner standing 8.8 in aft of the old fit too; the root lies 95 in down the 20 deg cant from the tip (BL 38.9, on the nacelle's shoulder)

surfaces.unit: BL in; the rudder as fractions of the fin's span from its root
surfaces.where: figure 2 (control surfaces labelled in the top and side views)
surfaces.note: spans of the hinged surfaces: the leading-edge flaps split at the fold (tp209033 PDF page 17) and run from the LEX-wing junction to the tip; the flap's ends, the aileron's inner end and the rudder's are read off figure 2's sketch. The aileron runs to the tip (the sketch drew it ending at BL 220): with it drooped in dvids9820782 and dvids9820788, sky shows directly outboard of its end, under the tip's launcher rail. Each surface's chord fraction follows from its cr201687 area over these spans

gear.unit: FS in for the axle centres; WL in for the axles; in for the track (between the main wheels' centres) and the nose wheels' spacing
gear.where: NATOPS 1.1.2's heights for the axles; verify/photos.py over photos.json for the track and the nose wheels' spacing (the wheels' hub faces in 6-9 photos, +-0.4 in across); tp209033 figure 2 for the stations, which the photos confirm (FS 495.1 and 280.9, +-1.2)
gear.note: the wheel centres' stations from the nose apex on tp209033 figure 2 (FS 59.82 marked) at its 56 ft scale, wheelbase 17.77 ft. The axles' heights are set so NATOPS's static heights hold over the ground beneath the tyres (fins 15 ft 3 in, canopy 10 ft 6 in): the jet then sits 0.9 deg nose down. The photos' taxiing jets put the main axle 2.9 in higher (WL 44.3 +-1.5) and the nose axle 0.8 in higher (45.6 +-0.9), more nose down, as a lighter or moving jet may sit. The track and the nose wheels' spacing are the photos': the main hub faces stand 66.2 in either side and the nose hub faces 8.9 in, less a third of each tyre's width to its centre (tp209033's rear view drew the track 116 in). Tyre diameters from dvids9820808's matched camera; widths read off the gear close-ups dvids8678626 and dvids8678628 against those diameters

canopy.unit: FS in, WL in; the sill as [FS, WL, BL]; top, the canopy's top line behind the crown as [FS, WL]; glass, the exponents of the superellipse the glass's section follows from the sill to the top centreline, at the bow's foot and at the aft corner (linear between)
canopy.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): windscreen_base in 5 photos, bow_top 2, canopy_aft 3, bow_foot 4, sill_aft 4 (+-1 in); canopy_crown and the sill's middle in dvids9820808 alone. glass and top: the canopy outlines traced in the seven photos with well-solved cameras, split fore and aft by the station of the model's silhouette nearest each traced point, the cameras held while only the canopy changes. The glass's upper edge against the sky in the profiles dvids9820808 and dvids9820801 (the strongest step in each pixel column, cast onto the centreline) gives the top line behind the crown; the two agree within 0.15 in (0.45 at FS 264), three readings that caught the cockpit inside left out. With that top line the outlines' median miss is 0.28 in (1.00 with the cited sections unchanged): forward of FS 280 any exponent from 1.8 to 2.3 does as well, aft 1.0 and 1.2 do (0.20 and 0.25 in) while 1.6 and 2.0 miss by 0.55 and 0.83
canopy.note: the windscreen's front base, the bow between windscreen and canopy, the canopy's crown and aft end on the centreline, and the canopy's sill from the bow's foot to the canopy's aft lower corner. The cited sections between FS 184 and 253 leave the skin 2-2.5 in wider than the sill, so the build draws the glass in to meet it

eye.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json: dvids9820808's helmet located from its camera solved with the other 11 photos, centre FS 254.5 WL 154.4, top WL 159.3
eye.note: the design eye, provisional: a little ahead of and below the helmet's centre in the reference photo, where the pilot sits reaching for the canopy bow

hardpoints.where: Stores: the store elements' buttlines, which it takes from NATOPS figure 4-4
hardpoints.note: stations 1-9 (air-stores.md). Buttlines are the flight model's; the wing stations' mounts sit on the wing's lower surface at the chord fraction given, and the fuselage stations' on the skin straight below their station and buttline (the nacelle and the keel; the waterlines here are the flight model's), all provisional until the reference photos with stores are matched

lights.where: 2.6.1 (position, formation, strobe, approach, landing, hook and probe lights)
lights.note: what the jet carries and roughly where; every position here is provisional until the reference photos are matched, the position lights after the engine's own (LEX edge ahead of the wing root, under the wing at the fold)

lex.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): lex_apex in 7 photos (+-0.8 in); the fence's top corners in 3 photos (+-1.8 in)
lex.note: where the LEX's edge leaves the body, 7 in aft of and 5 in below where cr186938's graph extrapolates it (FS 189); and the top corners of the fleet LEX fence, which stands on tp3111's base (lex.fence: FS 378.17 to 410.33 at BL 42)

probe.unit: FS in; degrees from the top centreline
probe.where: the door's lower corners cast onto the skin: each solved camera's sight line through probe_door_front (dvids9820810, dvids9820801) and probe_door_aft (dvids9820808, dvids9820810, dvids9820801) meets the fuselage at WL 123.3-123.7 and 131.4-131.8 (38 and 36 deg round), FS 144.2-145.6 and 185.8-189.1. The upper edge: tm101724's (fittings.probe), theta 165 from the keel
probe.note: the reference airframe's probe door, shorter than the research jet's (fittings.probe, FS 128.5 to 188). The photos are all right-side views, so the bundle alone leaves the corners 3-4 in inside the skin along their sight lines; the skin fixes that depth. The upper edge is the research jet's, 15 deg round from the top: one solved photo sees it, dvids9820799 at a grazing 16 deg, casting it at BL 7.0-8.7 (and the lower edge at 11.5-13, against the corners' 12.2-14.4 on the skin), which so flat a view leaves uncertain by inches. An unsolved photo looking down on another jet (dvids3435192) agrees: it reads the edge 12-14 deg round, parallel to the centreline (BL 4.7-5.1 by its own calibration, which puts the lower edge 2-3 in inboard of the skin-cast one; scaled to that, BL 6.0-6.5 against the built 5.3-6.2); that jet's lower edge, 42 deg round, lies 5 deg below the photos'

aoa.unit: FS, WL in; the base plate's diameter, the cone's length and base diameter in
aoa.where: cast onto the skin: the right probe seen end-on in dvids9820808 (FS 164.4, WL 103.3), the left probe's base in dvids9820782 (FS 163.6, WL 103.8); its size read in dvids8678631 at 0.11 in per pixel, where the cone stands across the line of sight
aoa.note: the two angle-of-attack probes (natops 2.19.1), a cone standing straight out of each side of the nose on a round plate; both photos' projections land on the probes in dvids8678631 and dvids9820799

pitot.unit: FS, WL in; the tube's diameter in
pitot.where: dvids9820808: the strut's root cast onto the skin (BL 13.1), its bend and the tube's tip onto the root's buttline; the left tube in dvids9820782 and both in dvids9820799 lie where these project
pitot.note: the two pitot-static tubes under the nose (natops 2.12.1): a strut swept forward and down from the skin, the tube pointing forward from its foot. tm101724's FS 164 to 177 (fittings.pitot) agrees within 0.3 in

blisters.unit: [from FS, to FS, WL at the middle, width round the section, standing proud] in
blisters.where: ends and edges cast onto the skin: dvids9820808 (right) and dvids9820782 (left), which agree within 1 in of station and 2 in of waterline
blisters.note: antenna fairings on each side of the nose, above the formation light strip and on the gun bay's door; how far each stands proud is not measured, but taken in the ECM cover's proportion (fittings.ecm: 1.7 in on a 4 in width). The ECM covers are built from fittings.ecm, which the photos match (FS 128.2 to 137.5, centre WL 106.0, against tm101724's 129.3 to 138.8 and WL 105.7)

formation.where: the forward strip's ends and edges cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (right) and dvids9820782 (left), which agree within 0.6 in
formation.note: the electroluminescent formation light strips on each side of the nose (natops 2.6.1), flush with the skin

paint.unit: sRGB, 0-255; turn: the range of the surface normal's upward component over which the upper grey gives way to the lower
paint.where: dvids9820808, overcast: the mean of a clean patch of the fin's side (upper; 80 x 60 px at 1400-1480, 2350-2400, spread 3) and of the nose gear door's downward face (lower; 100 x 40 px at 5300-5400, 3080-3120, spread 5)
paint.note: the tactical greys, expected FS 36320 over 36375 (plan #8). The photo's light is in them: the lower grey faces away from the overcast sky and still reads 1.24 times as bright. The fins, whose outer faces tilt 20 deg down with their cant, keep the upper grey; the turn starts just below that

panels.unit: rings: stations of joints round the fuselage; lines: polylines of [FS, WL, BL] on the skin (mirrored ones are copied to the other side); width in; shade, the paint's brightness on a line
panels.where: the radome's joint cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (FS 127.9 to 128.1, top and bottom); tm101724's nose.junction gives 128.5. The lines, in order: fuselage_side_lower_right (mirrored), door_edge_359_right (mirrored), door_edge_327_right (mirrored), door_edge_287_right (mirrored), door_edge_234_right (mirrored), panel_edge_204_right, panel_edge_204_left_lower, panel_lower_234_204_right (mirrored), door_hinge_right (mirrored), latch_panel_right, access_panel_195_right, access_panel_175_right, access_door_left, sill_line_right (mirrored), spine_side_right (mirrored), spine_joint_335, spine_joint_385, spine_joint_422, spine_joint_456, spine_joint_491, spine_joint_521, fin_root_panel_right, fin_root_panel_left, fin_root_fillet_right (mirrored), nacelle_side_right (mirrored), afterbody_joint_right (mirrored): traced in dvids9820801, 9820808, 9820810, 9820782 and 9820788 and cast onto the skin (verify/cast.py), each checked in a second photo where one shows it (most within 0.1-1.3 in)
panels.note: the panel lines baked into the paint, about one and a half texels of the 2048 atlas wide (one texel aliases into dashes). The mirrored lines were traced on the right and copied to the left; one oblique left photo (9820782) puts the doors' edges at FS 234, 287 and 327 1-2.5 in further forward, unsettled. The spine joints' tops (10-12 in either side of the centreline) no photo sees: filled along the skin at the same station. The spine lines were cast from dvids9820801, which sees them nearly abeam: the model's spine aft of FS 440 is broader than the photos' (a task), so they need casting again when it changes. Single-photo: panel_edge_204_left_lower, spine_joint_385, fin_root_panel_left, nacelle_side_right, afterbody_joint_right

stencils.unit: at: [FS, WL] of the stencil's middle on each side's skin; size: [length along the stations, height] in; dark and light: the paint's brightness under the stencil's ink and its lettering
stencils.where: corners cast onto the skin in dvids9820808 (right): the warning box FS 299.4-319.4, WL 130.2-137.8; the triangle FS 274.7-283.9 at its top edge (WL 137.8), its point FS 278.7, WL 130.1. dvids9820782 shows the same pair on the left where they project. The ink and lettering against the paint round them, sRGB (43, 59, 75) and (104, 120, 138) against (115, 136, 150)
stencils.note: the ejection-seat warnings under the cockpit on each side (plan #8: the functional stencils stay); their text as the photos read it

cockpit.unit: [FS, WL] in on the centreline: the seat's headbox from its lower front corner round; the HUD frame's foot and top; the glareshield's aft edge
cockpit.where: dvids9820808, seen through the canopy and cast onto the centreline's plane (verify/cast.py)
cockpit.note: what the simple cockpit is placed by. Its widths, the tub's floor and walls, the instrument panel and the pilot's limbs are estimated round these and the canopy's sill: no source gives them, and the detailed cockpit (step 6) replaces all of it in first person

antennas.unit: dorsal and spine: [FS, WL] corners on the centreline, the base's front and aft, the tip's aft and front; dome: [FS, WL, BL, diameter, standing proud]; comb: the stations of the posts under the nose; chin: [from FS, to FS, standing proud] of the fairing under the radome; in
antennas.where: dvids9820808 cast onto the centreline (the blades, the comb and the chin fairing); dvids9820782 sees the blades from the left on the centreline, and the dome on the upper left, cast onto the skin (FS 439.8-447.9, WL 145.4, BL -12.2 to -13.1); dvids9820808 shows no dome on the right
antennas.note: the dorsal blade antennas, the dome antenna on the left of the spine, and the small antennas under the radome. The dome's width and height, the blades' thickness and the comb posts' size are estimated

pod.where: dvids9820808, the right fin's pod cast onto the fin's plane (BL 69); dvids9820782 shows the left fin's alike
pod.note: the antenna fairing on each fin's trailing edge below the tip, on the fixed fin above the rudder: a pod straddling the fin, its blunt end at the trailing edge, 8.6 in below the tip

blade.unit: FS in; the bottom edge as [from FS, to FS, WL] in
blade.where: dvids9820808, cast onto the centreline's plane; dvids9820799, seen from ahead, puts it on the centreline within its chord
blade.note: the blade antenna under the nose ahead of the nose gear (stencilled DO NOT PAINT). Its thickness is not measured

hook.where: dvids9820808: the stowed hook's shank (pivot from the old single-photo locate, point solved with the 12 photos, +-2 in)
hook.note: the stowed hook: its pivot forward and its point aft (dvids9820748 shows it lowered, trailing aft from the pivot). One photo shows the point stowed: provisional

nozzle.unit: FS in; radius in at start and exit; WL in of the axis
nozzle.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (12 photos solved together): nozzle_exit_bottom in 4 photos (FS 720.0 +-2, WL 90.45 +-2.1)
nozzle.note: the nozzles' outer flaps on the engine axes: the exit's lower lip where the photos put it; the HARV's exhaust plane (overall.exhaust) stands 7 in further forward. The start and the start's radius are provisional (fitted to the HATP views)

petals.unit: outer flaps per nozzle; in, the exit lip's move from open to closed; in, the throat's radius closed (military) and open (full reheat)
petals.where: the count from the three photos (both nozzles of one jet end-on, 12 brackets each; a second jet's 12 trailing-edge gaps; a third's flap tabs 30 deg apart); tm101741 printed page 3 for the nozzle areas, 220 in2 at military power and 348 in2 at full reheat; tm88273 printed page 4 for the 12 primary flaps and 12 seals inside
petals.note: the throat's radii are the areas' circles; the outer flaps' exit lip is taken to move in as far as the throat does (provisional: no source gives the outer flaps' own travel). The parked photos show the nozzles open; the HARV (tm101724's jet) had its outer flaps removed

inlet.unit: [FS, WL, BL] in; lip: its rounded front edge's highest, lowest and most outboard points and the ends of its curve at the flat inboard wall, outer side; outline: [WL, BL] along the lip's front edge from the top corner round the outside to the bottom corner; splitter: its leading edge, top to bottom
inlet.where: verify/photos.py over photos.json (15 photos solved together): the lip's and splitter's points in 2 to 4 of dvids9820748, dvids9820788, dvids8678631 and dvids9820808 each (+-0.7 to 1.9 in); the outline from the three lip traces cast onto the lip's plane (they agree within 1.5 in); the splitter's leading edge from dvids9820808 and dvids8678631 together (dvids9820748 and dvids9820788 agree within 0.7 in); the wall is the lip rim's width in dvids9820748 (10-15 px, 1.0 to 1.3 in). The lip's lower and outboard points, and its bottom corner, rest on one photo each outside the two 45 degree quarter views (dvids8678631, dvids9820808): leaving that photo out moves them up to 12 in along the quarter views' line of sight, so a mistake in its mark would go unseen there; the three lip traces cast onto the lip's plane from three cameras agree within 1.5 in, which they would not if the plane were wrong
inlet.note: the lip stands 40 in aft of where the model first had it (FS 365), under the LEX-wing junction, raked 3.5 in aft from top to bottom, its flat inboard side leaning inboard at the bottom; tp3478's FS 401 section (figure 4a) shows the splitter plate there but no duct yet, which agrees. The duct inside the measured lip has a hydraulic diameter of 23.6 in, tm103703's 23.34 (engine.inlet). The splitter's leading edge stands upright at FS 381, bowing 2.7 in outboard at mid-height

nacelle.unit: keel: the stations over which each nacelle's bottom follows the HATP side view's keel line (references/profiles.json, smoothed as build.py reads it), eased onto it from the lip's bottom (layout.inlet); aft: [FS, WL] knots on to the nozzles; photo: [FS, WL, uncertainty] where an in-flight photo's outline reads the bottom
nacelle.where: the HATP figure's side view keel line between FS 436 and 620 (WL 73.3 at FS 448-452, 75.8 at 500, 78.3 at 540, 85.0 at 620); dvids6696790's lower outline, a sky silhouette behind the left lip, with its camera solved among 21 photos (verify/photos.py, 7.0 px): the skin steps 0.8 in below the lip's rim right behind it and falls to WL 73.6 at FS 447 cast onto BL -29 (+-1.5 in: the camera stands 7 deg above the wing plane), where an AIM-120's radome takes the outline over; navy090707N7665E003's lit strip along the right nacelle's lower side, seen from below (3.5 px), falls at the same slope over the first 25-30 in, bottoms out near FS 490-500 and rises 2-2.5 in by FS 509-528. aft: the earlier section's bottom, where the line rises past the hook and the nozzles (the HATP line reads 87.5 at FS 640)
nacelle.note: the nacelles hang about 10 in below the belly between them (the central body's bottom, WL 84). The earlier build held each nacelle's bottom at WL 87, from a symmetric section fitted to the HATP views, and rose 10 in behind the lip into it: the photos and the line both fall instead. The build keeps each nacelle's section above its centre as it was (its shoulder meets the wing's root there) and reaches below the centre down to this line. The navy photo's strip reads 2-2.5 in below the line all along, since it cannot fix its buttline (6 in of buttline there looks like 2.5 in of waterline): it agrees with the line's shape, not its level. dvids9820808's tank below the right nacelle cannot place the line (which tank it is, centreline or station 7, is not settled, and the open gear doors hang across the nacelle's lower edge), and the other solved ground photos are in shade or behind tanks
